validated_results.title: Meat consumption, cooking practices, meat mutagens, and risk of prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: This population-based case-control study provides multivariable-adjusted odds ratios and trend p-values for the association between processed meat intake and risk of advanced prostate cancer.

extraction.population: Population-based sample of men aged 40-79 years residing in the San Francisco Bay Area

sample_size.location: Section: Statistical Analysis, Paragraph 2; total_n derived from reported group counts 531 + 527 = 1058

cases.excerpt: Newly diagnosed cases aged 40–79 years (531 advanced cases, 195 localized cases) and 527 controls were asked about dietary intake, including usual meat cooking methods and doneness levels.

effect_size.excerpt: Additional adjustment for dietary variables attenuated these associations somewhat; significant trends and/or elevated ORs for high consumption remained for red meat (OR=1.53, 95% CI=0.93–2.49, p trend =0.02), hamburger (OR=1.79, 95% CI=1.10–2.92, p trend =0.005), steak (OR=1.45 (95% CI=0.89–2.35, p trend =0.05), and processed meat (OR=1.57, 95% CI=1.04–2.36, p trend =0.05). For red meat, risk varied by cooking method and doneness level ( Table 3 ).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Additional adjustment for dietary variables attenuated these associations somewhat; significant trends and/or elevated ORs for high consumption remained for red meat (OR=1.53, 95% CI=0.93–2.49, p trend =0.02), hamburger (OR=1.79, 95% CI=1.10–2.92, p trend =0.005), steak (OR=1.45 (95% CI=0.89–2.35, p trend =0.05), and processed meat (OR=1.57, 95% CI=1.04–2.36, p trend =0.05).

design.excerpt: We assessed the association with meat consumption and estimated HCA and PAH exposure in a population-based case-control study of prostate cancer.

timing.excerpt: Usual dietary intake (during the calendar year prior to diagnosis for cases and prior to selection into the study for controls) was assessed using a 74-item food frequency questionnaire (FFQ)
